annotation.title_clean: Commission Staff Working Document: Impact Assessment accompanying the Proposal for a Regulation laying down harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
annotation.title_en: Commission Staff Working Document: Impact Assessment accompanying the Proposal for a Regulation laying down harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Commission impact assessment for the proposed EU AI Act. It identifies six problems (safety, fundamental rights, enforcement gaps, legal uncertainty, mistrust, fragmentation) and compares four policy options. It favours a horizontal, risk-based regime with mandatory requirements for high-risk AI. Physical AI appears mainly through product-safety links to machinery, vehicles and medical devices.
key_provisions_or_claims: Identifies six problems driven by AI opacity, complexity, adaptation, autonomy and data dependency.
Compares four options: voluntary labelling, sectoral approach, horizontal mandatory rules for high-risk AI (3/3+), and rules for all AI.
Favours Option 3+: mandatory requirements for high-risk AI plus codes of conduct for others.
Product-safety legislation (Machinery, medical devices, vehicles) is revised separately; AI Act complements it.
Liability rules and the Product Liability Directive are left to a separate follow-up initiative; exclusive military AI is out of scope.
